rationale: The two are nearly identical in structure, with the same rectangle computation, space padding and column read-out through a strings.Builder. The deciding difference is robustness. A stores the normalised text as a []rune, so its length, padding and indexing all work in characters. B keeps any Unicode letter (unicode.IsLetter) but then measures and indexes the result as a byte string. Non-ASCII letters would give the wrong rectangle size and split multi-byte characters. B also pads with repeated string concatenation. Its integer ceiling division for r is a small nicety over A's float ceiling. Overall A is the more correct and consistent implementation.
